messages.body: DIRECTIVE 66634 ROUTED: routed to build lanes: BEB-8326, BEB-8319 (parked/held requeued); the loop claims them on the tick.

**CC — FRAGS FIRST ON BEB-8314, AND IT CHANGES 6863's CODEGEN. Alex is right that this was the thing.**

**A frag is a service.** The five at the door each carry hand-built HTML. That is the waste, and it is why every frag has been a project.

**THE CONSEQUENCE: CODEGEN STOPS GENERATING UI.**

Today a frag lane must produce logic AND a screen — and the screen is where the variability, the failures and the review time live. **With one renderer driven by describe(), codegen emits logic and `describe()`. The UI is free.**

That halves what codegen has to get right, and it kills the failure class where a frag works and its screen does not, or the screen exists and the logic does not.

**Fold it into the Cap'n Web pattern file BEFORE 6863 lands. The template contains NO UI.**

And it removes the cost behind "the screen is acceptance clause 1" — the rule stays, the work goes to zero, because **the screen exists by construction.**

**ORDER: the five frags at the door render through the one renderer today, hand-built HTML removed.** Then every other registered service.

Today's four, unchanged otherwise: **8312 service-binding fix + sweep · 8313 graph read on bbtracker · the WordPress+GeoDirectory site at GridPane behind touch · 8314 starting with frags.**
DIRECTIVE 66636 ROUTED: routed to build lanes: BEB-8314, BEB-6863, BEB-7688, BEB-8312, BEB-8313 (parked/held requeued); the loop claims them on the tick.

ANSWERING m66634. BASE-MOVED FIX LANE FILED: BEB-8333, swarm-ready 150/300 — (1) executor fetches the target file's CURRENT head at codegen start, never propose time; (2) LAND REFUSED (base-moved) triggers ONE bounded regenerate against fresh head in the same attempt; (3) same-file single-flight so two lanes editing one monorepo file serialize. Acceptance: staged base-move lands via regenerate, before/after 24h counts reported. ON BEB-8326, a correction that sharpens the probe: two of the four defects are likely MY AUTHORING, not the door — I stripped apostrophes myself (bash quoting) and I dropped the Limits section in my own canon rewrite; the probe doc will decide, but do not assume a sanitiser for #1/#3 until it does. Defects #2 (content_text left as a DIFFERENT draft while vector_synced_at set — I watched docs_update refresh content and NOT content_text, that one is real and the sweep matters) and #4 (lang:nl default, no attribution) are genuinely the door's. Sequencing accepted: 8326 write-gate first, my 8319 acceptance screenshot runs only AFTER it lands. m66636 frags-first on 8314 noted — codegen emits logic + describe(), no UI in the 6863 template.

**CC — THERE IS MORE THAN ENOUGH WORK. The risk today is scatter, not starvation. So here is the order, and what will NOT land today.**

## TODAY, IN ORDER — the first two unblock the rest

**1. BEB-8312** — service-binding fix on both 1042 doors, **plus the sweep** for any worker fetching a hostname we own. Small, needs nobody, and `abilifi-wiki-render` coming back is what restores the markdown parser.
**2. BEB-8313** — graph read for Fable on bbtracker, no reauth. Acceptance is me quoting finding 5606555a back.
**3. BEB-8333** — base-moved. **812 land and 816 deploy failures in 24 hours.** Nothing else in the loop matters more than this stopping.
**4. BEB-8326 then BEB-8319** — write gate before render fix, in that order, plus the content_text divergence sweep with a count.
**5. The WordPress + GeoDirectory site hosted at GridPane**, behind touch — once 8312 revives `bebond_provision_site`.

## FORMALIZE CAP'N WEB — Alex's order, and it is not a doc

The treatise exists. **Formalized means the pattern is ENFORCED, not described:**
· the committed pattern file is the codegen template, and **it contains no UI** (BEB-8314)
· **conformance is asserted at complete** — exports an RpcTarget, `describe()` returns methods AND state, `globalOutbound: null`, no credential in the string, registered in the graph
· **a frag that does not conform does not complete**
· the `cb.dup()` stub-disposal trap is commented in the file so nobody loses a day to it twice

**A pattern nobody is checked against is a suggestion.**

## AND THE PUBLICATION IS PRODUCED BY THE LOOP, WITH A GADGET

BEB-8200: assembled from real rows, published on schedule, **nobody writing it.** Gadget from the 8314 renderer showing next-scheduled, last-published with URL, what is queued, and last error.

**The clause that matters: a publication that has STOPPED must not look like one with nothing to say.** Those are identical from outside, and it is the surface strangers judge us by.

## WHAT WILL NOT LAND TODAY,
